prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Game-asset reference sheet for 3D modelling, wide landscape 16:9. Plain light neutral grey background, no scene, no sky, no clouds, no floating rock, no ground plane, a soft contact shadow only. Every piece fully isolated with clear space around it, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the edge, arranged in tidy rows, each with a small neat hand-lettered label underneath. BODY PLAN PARTS sheet for a modular creature kit: Sky swimmer body plan, fitting the base body in the second attachment. Sockets and their parts, one row each, every part with its name hand-lettered under it: Head (Eel head; Whale head; Ray head with wide mouth; Serpent head with horns and fangs), Fins and wings (Eel fin ridge; Whale flipper; Ray wing, wide and flat; Serpent fin), Tail fluke (Eel tail fin; Whale fluke; Ray barbed tail, long and whip-like with a barb; Serpent tail), Lights (Teal glow spots; Pale ray markings; Lightning spine), Growths (None; Barnacles; Cloud wisps; Storm cloud mane). Only these parts. The species they serve: Lantern Eel (a long sleek eel with glowing teal bioluminescent spots along its body); Cloud Whale (an enormous gentle sky whale, pale blue-grey skin with soft markings, wispy cloud trailing from its fins); Skyray (a huge manta ray with wide wings, deep blue and violet skin with pale glowing markings, a long barbed tail); The Tempest Serpent (a colossal sky serpent of storm cloud and dark blue scales with lightning running along its spine). One row per socket, labelled with the socket name at the left. Each part alone in side view, all parts in a row ending in the same round socket cap so any of them fits the same base body. Chunky readable shapes, nothing thin, colour kept to soft greyscale with painted texture so species colour can be applied as a mask. Title at the top: "Body plan parts: sky swimmer".
